# AI Inbx

> Email infrastructure for software that holds conversations. Send, receive, thread, and reply over one API.

## Integrate AI Inbx

Use AI Inbx to send and receive email, connect mailboxes, and reply in threads. REST base: https://api.aiinbx.com/api/v2. TypeScript: npm install aiinbx. Python: pip install aiinbx. Read the quickstart, API reference, and production guide before implementing. Keep keys server-side, verify webhooks over the raw body, and persist an idempotency key and payload for each logical send.

## Docs

- [AI Inbx documentation](https://docs.aiinbx.com/): Learn to send and receive email, manage conversation threads, and build AI email agents with the AI Inbx API, TypeScript SDK, and Python SDK.
- [Quickstart](https://docs.aiinbx.com/quickstart): Get started with AI Inbx: add a sending domain, send your first email with the SDK, and receive the reply through a verified webhook.
- [Core concepts](https://docs.aiinbx.com/concepts): The building blocks of AI Inbx: workspaces, sending identities, emails, threads, events, and the spaces that keep each customer's mail apart.
- [Authentication](https://docs.aiinbx.com/authentication): Authenticate with Bearer API keys: the three scopes and what each one reaches, how to keep keys server-side, and how to rotate and delete them.
- [Going to production](https://docs.aiinbx.com/guides/production): Go to production with AI Inbx: reliable, idempotent sends, durable webhook processing, customer boundaries, and monitoring of delivery outcomes.
- [Plans and billing](https://docs.aiinbx.com/guides/billing): What each plan includes, exactly what counts against it, how extra usage and spending caps work, and what the API answers at a limit.

## Sending

- [Sending](https://docs.aiinbx.com/guides/sending): Addresses, HTML and text bodies, attachments, custom headers, idempotency, and what the send response tells you.
- [Scheduling](https://docs.aiinbx.com/guides/scheduling): Schedule a send up to 30 days ahead, move it, or cancel it, and learn what stays editable on a scheduled email until the moment it goes out.
- [Drafts](https://docs.aiinbx.com/guides/drafts): Let an agent write an email and a person decide: create drafts over the API, then review, edit and send them from the console or your own UI.
- [Suppressions](https://docs.aiinbx.com/guides/suppressions): Lists that stop the next send — bounces, complaints, unsubscribes — scoped per campaign or across the whole workspace.
- [Pacing](https://docs.aiinbx.com/guides/pacing): Pace outbound mail with sending hours and rate ceilings, see the queue they hold messages in, and inspect, release or override held sends.

## Receiving

- [Receiving](https://docs.aiinbx.com/guides/receiving): Two ways mail reaches your code — an MX record on a domain, or a connected Gmail or Outlook mailbox — and what arrives when it does.
- [Threads](https://docs.aiinbx.com/guides/threads): Read a conversation, page through a long one, and reply or forward within a thread without reconstructing In-Reply-To or References headers.
- [Attachments](https://docs.aiinbx.com/guides/attachments): Download what arrived, or read the prepared Markdown of each attachment so a model can use a PDF or a document without you running a parser.

## Addresses

- [Domains](https://docs.aiinbx.com/guides/domains): Add a sending domain, publish the DNS records, verify it, diagnose the one record that won't resolve, and cover every subdomain at once with a wildcard.
- [Mailboxes](https://docs.aiinbx.com/guides/mailboxes): Connect existing Gmail or Outlook accounts over OAuth from a hosted page, a link or the API, keep them synced, and brand the consent screen.
- [Spaces](https://docs.aiinbx.com/guides/spaces): Group a workspace's domains, mailboxes and mail by customer — one space each — with rules and suppression lists that reach that space alone.

## Webhooks

- [Webhooks](https://docs.aiinbx.com/webhooks): Register an endpoint, choose events, route them by address, and understand what happens when a delivery fails.
- [Verifying](https://docs.aiinbx.com/webhooks/verifying): Verify AI Inbx webhook signatures: the HMAC-SHA256 scheme, verifying in the TypeScript and Python SDKs, and checking it by hand in any language.

### Events

- [Event reference](https://docs.aiinbx.com/webhooks/events): Every AI Inbx webhook event type, the envelope they share, what each one means, and how to handle email, thread, domain and mailbox events.
- [email.received](https://docs.aiinbx.com/webhooks/events/email-received): email.received fires once per inbound message, already matched onto its thread. The event most AI Inbx applications are built around.
- [email.sent](https://docs.aiinbx.com/webhooks/events/email-sent): email.sent fires when a message is handed to the mail provider: acceptance, not delivery. A full endpoint gets the whole email with it.
- [email.delivered](https://docs.aiinbx.com/webhooks/events/email-delivered): email.delivered fires when the receiving server accepts a message, per recipient. It does not prove inbox placement or that anyone read it.
- [email.bounced](https://docs.aiinbx.com/webhooks/events/email-bounced): email.bounced fires when delivery fails for good, hard or soft. Each recipient comes with a cause, and a dead address is suppressed, so the next send to it never leaves.
- [email.complained](https://docs.aiinbx.com/webhooks/events/email-complained): email.complained fires when a recipient marks your message as spam. Rarer than a bounce and far more serious for your sending reputation.
- [email.failed](https://docs.aiinbx.com/webhooks/events/email-failed): email.failed fires when the mail provider refuses a message before any delivery attempt: nothing reached a recipient and nothing is retried.
- [email.unsubscribed](https://docs.aiinbx.com/webhooks/events/email-unsubscribed): email.unsubscribed fires when a recipient opts out by link, one-click header or reply, naming the suppression list and scope it was written to.
- [email.opened](https://docs.aiinbx.com/webhooks/events/email-opened): email.opened fires on a tracked open, with bot and privacy-proxy hits flagged. Requires open tracking on the domain or on the send.
- [email.clicked](https://docs.aiinbx.com/webhooks/events/email-clicked): email.clicked fires when a recipient follows a tracked link, a far stronger engagement signal than an open. Bot and scanner hits are flagged.
- [thread.created](https://docs.aiinbx.com/webhooks/events/thread-created): thread.created fires when a new conversation starts: from an inbound message, a send that joined no thread, or a forward.
- [domain.verified](https://docs.aiinbx.com/webhooks/events/domain-verified): domain.verified fires when a domain's DKIM identity is verified and it can send. Use it to offer the domain as a sender in your product.
- [domain.at_risk](https://docs.aiinbx.com/webhooks/events/domain-at-risk): domain.at_risk fires when a verified domain's DKIM record goes missing from DNS. The domain still sends; if the record is not back by stops_sending_at, 72 hours later, the domain is lost.
- [domain.restored](https://docs.aiinbx.com/webhooks/events/domain-restored): domain.restored fires when a domain's missing DKIM record has been back in DNS for an hour before the domain was lost. The domain signs as before.
- [domain.lost](https://docs.aiinbx.com/webhooks/events/domain-lost): domain.lost fires when a verified domain's DKIM record has been missing from DNS for 72 hours: sends from it fail with domain_unverified until the record is back.
- [mailbox.connected](https://docs.aiinbx.com/webhooks/events/mailbox-connected): mailbox.connected fires when a customer finishes authorizing a Gmail or Outlook mailbox, carrying your ref and metadata to match it to a user.
- [mailbox.needs_reauth](https://docs.aiinbx.com/webhooks/events/mailbox-needs-reauth): mailbox.needs_reauth fires when a mailbox's stored authorization stops working: revoked access, a password change, or an admin policy.
- [mailbox.disconnected](https://docs.aiinbx.com/webhooks/events/mailbox-disconnected): mailbox.disconnected fires when a mailbox is removed, by you over the API or by the customer revoking access at Google or Microsoft.

## Integrate

- [Integrate AI Inbx](https://docs.aiinbx.com/integrations): Integrate AI Inbx with your stack: Next.js and Hono webhook handlers, React Email templates, and agent loops that send, read and reply to mail.
- [Next.js](https://docs.aiinbx.com/integrations/nextjs): Use AI Inbx in Next.js: a route handler that verifies and receives webhooks, and a server action that sends email with the TypeScript SDK.
- [Hono](https://docs.aiinbx.com/integrations/hono): Receive AI Inbx webhooks in Hono on Cloudflare Workers, Bun, Deno and Node: verify the signature over the raw body and hand the event to a worker.
- [React Email](https://docs.aiinbx.com/integrations/react-email): Send React Email templates through AI Inbx: pass a component as `react` and the TypeScript SDK renders its HTML. Keep passing `text` beside it.
- [Build an AI email agent](https://docs.aiinbx.com/integrations/agents): Build an AI email agent with signed webhooks, conversation threads, human review, and idempotent replies using the AI Inbx TypeScript SDK.

## MCP & CLI

- [MCP server](https://docs.aiinbx.com/mcp): Run AI Inbx from Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code, Codex or any MCP client, or give it an inbox of its own: two servers, signed in as you or with an API key.
- [MCP tools](https://docs.aiinbx.com/mcp/tools): Every tool the AI Inbx MCP servers offer, with its arguments and what a client is told about it before it runs.
- [CLI](https://docs.aiinbx.com/cli): The aiinbx command line: send and read mail, call every API resource, forward webhooks to localhost without a tunnel, and check a domain's DNS.
- [Give your agent an inbox](https://docs.aiinbx.com/guides/agent-inbox): Connect Claude Code, Cursor or the aiinbx CLI to an inbox — an email address of its own that it sends from and reads, and nothing else in your workspace.
- [Documentation for agents](https://docs.aiinbx.com/reference/agents): Machine-readable docs for coding agents: llms.txt, Markdown copies of every page, the OpenAPI document, and the rules for implementing AI Inbx.

## SDKs

- [SDKs](https://docs.aiinbx.com/sdks): Official TypeScript and Python clients — same resources, same idempotency and webhook verification, idiomatic in each language.
- [TypeScript](https://docs.aiinbx.com/sdks/typescript): Install, configure, and use the aiinbx package — resources, pagination, response metadata, typed errors, React Email, and webhook verification.
- [Python](https://docs.aiinbx.com/sdks/python): Install, configure, and use the aiinbx package — sync and async clients, pagination, raw responses, typed errors, and webhook verification.

## Reference

- [Conventions](https://docs.aiinbx.com/reference/conventions): The rules that hold across every AI Inbx endpoint: prefixed IDs, cursor pagination, timestamps, request IDs, and idempotent retries.
- [Errors](https://docs.aiinbx.com/reference/errors): Every AI Inbx error code in the problem+json body, what each one means, how to recover from it, and which failures are worth retrying.

- [agent-readability.json](https://docs.aiinbx.com/agent-readability.json): Manifest of every agent-facing artifact on this site.
